title: Aft Cargo Compartment Smoke Sampling Ports — Detailed Inspection and Flow Check
abstract: Detailed inspection of the two aft hold smoke sampling ports and a flow check of the sampling tubes, with the labyrinth drain check at the shielded inlet.

sections.purpose: This task gives the detailed inspection of the aft cargo compartment smoke sampling ports and the flow check of each sampling tube, at the scheduled interval or after any unexplained detection event.
sections.job_setup_note: The aircraft must be on the ground with the cargo hold empty and the compartment lighting on. Put the safety barriers in position at the cargo door. Get the flow check gauge, the borescope and the smoke generator.
sections.procedure: 1. Open the aft cargo door and put the safety barriers in position. 2. Remove the ceiling lining panels at the two sampling positions. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of each port for obstruction, damage and loose fixing. 4. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sampling tube for chafing where it crosses the ceiling rail. 5. Disconnect the sampling tube at the regulator and connect the flow check gauge. 6. Record the flow at each port. It must be between 24 and 36 litres per minute. 7. Examine the labyrinth drain of each shielded inlet with the borescope and confirm it is clear. 8. CAUTION: DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAR A BLOCKED DRAIN. THE LABYRINTH WILL BE DAMAGED. 9. Reconnect the sampling tube at the regulator. 10. WARNING: TELL THE FLIGHT COMPARTMENT BEFORE YOU RELEASE SMOKE INTO THE COMPARTMENT. THE WARNING IS TRANSMITTED TO THE FLIGHT DECK AND CAN CAUSE AN UNWANTED DISCHARGE. 11. Do the detection functional check with the smoke generator at each port and record the response time. 12. Refit the ceiling lining panels.
sections.close_out: Clear the detection warning at the flight compartment and confirm the system returns to normal. Make sure the compartment is clean and the barriers are removed. Record the flow values, the response times and the drain condition in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Put the safety barriers in position at the cargo door.
Tell the flight compartment before smoke is released into the compartment.

issue.reason: Effectivity of the labyrinth drain check written into the step, the job setup note and the effectivity statement, and a not-applicable recording rule added for the open port.

abstract: Detailed inspection of the two aft hold smoke sampling ports and a flow check of the sampling tubes, with the drain check that applies to aircraft carrying the shielded inlet.

sections.purpose: This task gives the detailed inspection of the aft cargo compartment smoke sampling ports and the flow check of each sampling tube, at the scheduled interval or after any unexplained detection event.
sections.job_setup_note: The aircraft must be on the ground with the cargo hold empty and the compartment lighting on. Put the safety barriers in position at the cargo door. Get the flow check gauge, the borescope and the smoke generator. Establish the sampling port standard from the aircraft configuration record before you start: the drain check in step 7 exists only on the shielded inlet. On an aircraft with the shielded inlet that step is mandatory; on an aircraft with the open port there is no labyrinth to examine, and the step must be recorded as not applicable rather than as a pass. A line engineer working a mixed fleet cannot tell the two apart from the compartment floor and the earlier wording did not say so plainly enough.
sections.procedure: 1. Open the aft cargo door and put the safety barriers in position. 2. Remove the ceiling lining panels at the two sampling positions. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of each port for obstruction, damage and loose fixing. 4. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sampling tube for chafing where it crosses the ceiling rail. 5. Disconnect the sampling tube at the regulator and connect the flow check gauge. 6. Record the flow at each port. It must be between 24 and 36 litres per minute. 7. POST MOD-168024 AIRCRAFT ONLY: examine the labyrinth drain of each shielded inlet with the borescope and confirm it is clear. On a pre MOD-168024 aircraft the port is open and has no labyrinth drain; enter NOT APPLICABLE against this step and go to step 9. 8. CAUTION: DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAR A BLOCKED DRAIN. THE LABYRINTH WILL BE DAMAGED. 9. Reconnect the sampling tube at the regulator. 10. WARNING: TELL THE FLIGHT COMPARTMENT BEFORE YOU RELEASE SMOKE INTO THE COMPARTMENT. THE WARNING IS TRANSMITTED TO THE FLIGHT DECK AND CAN CAUSE AN UNWANTED DISCHARGE. 11. Do the detection functional check with the smoke generator at each port and record the response time. 12. Refit the ceiling lining panels.
sections.close_out: Clear the detection warning at the flight compartment and confirm the system returns to normal. Make sure the compartment is clean and the barriers are removed. Record the flow values, the response times and the drain condition in the aircraft technical log. Where the aircraft is pre MOD-168024, the drain entry must read NOT APPLICABLE; a drain recorded as clear on an aircraft that has no drain has been the source of more than one false configuration record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft for steps 1 to 6 and 9 to 12. Step 7, the labyrinth drain check, applies to post MOD-168024 aircraft only and is recorded as not applicable on every other aircraft.

safety_precautions: Put the safety barriers in position at the cargo door.
Tell the flight compartment before smoke is released into the compartment.
